geometry_edits.rationale: Increase separation between wings to sharpen the public void and improve access-edge legibility.
Preserve a grounded connector so the split reads as a usable entry seam rather than detached fragments.
Keep the opening aligned with the program-frame access side.

graph_edits.rationale: Slightly widen the split to make the public threshold more legible at the access edge without losing the dominant split-wing gesture.
Keep the lower connector active so the void reads as an occupied public seam rather than a purely decorative gap.
Maintain the access-aligned opening toward the verified frontage side in the program frame.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent split-wing neighborhood mass with one dominant gesture and a legible central void/threshold. It responds to the parcel as a compact, directional object rather than merely filling a box, and the blue access edge is addressed by the split and notch-like ground opening. The silhouette is not especially refined in section, but it remains continuous enough to support the program and the public edge requirement. It is stronger as early-stage massing than as a finished form, with some risk of feeling a little boxy and compressed in section.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Curved roof/parapet language is not present in the candidate; use the spatial organization, not the silhouette.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part low-rise composition with a central void and bridge-like connector, keeping the street edge legible while making the void the organizing figure.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Scale is more expansive and multi-building than this compact candidate; do not copy the tower/podium condition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like sequencing of mass and courtyard can support neighborhood programs when the void reads as public open space rather than leftover subtraction.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is more compact and less rectilinear in presentation; avoid overemphasizing transparency or facade cues.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A large central cutout with an overhanging upper volume can create a strong public threshold and active ground condition.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is much smaller and more mass-driven; roof attachment/greenhouse language is not relevant here.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Horizontal spread with a courtyard void and slightly folded/terraced roof can strengthen program hierarchy without becoming a generic box.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate does not show as much section depth or roof variety; keep the simpler split-wing logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Connected wings around a core, with terraced or bridged circulation, fit neighborhood living well and preserve a clear dominant gesture.

warnings: The top/section is still fairly flat and could benefit from a clearer roof or daylight logic if further developed.
The access response is present but somewhat modest; the ground seam could be made more explicit if the next iteration needs stronger public legibility.
